description.short_caption: Axial MRI of the brain showing abnormal signal in the right frontal lobe.
description.detailed_description: This is an axial T1-weighted MRI image of the brain. There is an abnormal hypointense lesion in the right frontal lobe, with surrounding edema visible as a hypointense area. The ventricles appear midline, and no significant mass effect or midline shift is evident. The image is de-identified and suitable for educational purposes.
visible_findings: hypointense lesion in the right frontal lobe

description.short_caption: Axial MRI of the brain showing abnormal findings.
description.detailed_description: This is an axial T2-weighted MRI image of the brain. There is evidence of hyperintense lesions in the white matter, particularly in the periventricular regions. The lesions are asymmetrical and suggestive of a pathological process, possibly demyelination or infection. The ventricles appear slightly prominent, and there is no obvious midline shift.

description.short_caption: Coronal MRI of the brain with contrast showing abnormal enhancement.
description.detailed_description: This is a coronal MRI image of the brain obtained with contrast. The image demonstrates abnormal enhancement in the left hemisphere, suggestive of a focal lesion. The ventricles appear slightly asymmetrical, and there is evidence of mass effect with possible midline shift. The contrast highlights areas of disrupted blood-brain barrier, which could indicate infection, inflammation, or neoplasm.
visible_findings: abnormal contrast enhancement in the left hemisphere

Case_05007/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Gram stain of an aspirate from a subdural collection.

description.short_caption: Gram stain showing mixed bacterial morphology from a subdural collection aspirate.
description.detailed_description: This Gram stain image shows numerous bacterial forms, including gram-positive cocci in clusters and gram-negative bacilli. The background appears to have cellular debris, consistent with an aspirate from an infected site. The mixed morphology suggests a polymicrobial infection, which is common in subdural empyemas. The staining technique highlights the differential uptake of crystal violet and safranin by bacterial cell walls.

description.short_caption: Gram stain showing gram-positive and gram-negative bacilli.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a gram stain with a mix of gram-positive (purple) and gram-negative (pink) bacilli. The organisms are scattered throughout the field, with no clear clustering or specific arrangement. The background is clear, suggesting a clean preparation. The image is likely from a microbiological specimen, such as a clinical sample or culture.
